"BIG CRACK LAB – Complete Game Development Prompt

1. Game Overview

Create a 2.5D third-person survival, exploration, and mining simulator called BIG CRACK LAB.

The player works at a remote industrial research facility built on a flat grassland. Their main objective is to operate a massive drilling machine, dig deeper into Earth, earn money, purchase upgrades, manage oil supplies, and survive mysterious nighttime power interruptions caused by a monster.

The game should look polished, immersive, slightly mysterious, and colorful without excessive visual effects.

2. Graphics and Visual Style

- 2.5D third-person perspective.
- Stylized realistic low-poly 3D graphics.
- Vibrant but balanced colors.
- Detailed industrial buildings and machinery.
- Realistic lighting and shadows.
- Smooth animations.
- Dynamic day and night cycle.
- High-quality environmental atmosphere.

3. Map and Environment

Create a limited-sized, completely flat grassy environment.

Do not add mountains, hills, or complicated terrain.

The map must contain:

1. BIG CRACK LAB – A large two-story industrial research laboratory.
2. Main Mining Rig – A massive drilling machine inspired by the Kola Superdeep Borehole drilling equipment.
3. Oil Station – A separate building where players purchase oil.
4. Security Control Room – A room containing multiple CCTV monitors.
5. Industrial roads – Concrete paths connecting all buildings.
6. Fences, streetlights, electrical poles, warning signs, and storage containers.

Make the environment detailed but not overcrowded.

4. Player Controls

Mobile

- Virtual joystick on the bottom-left.
- Camera control on the right side.
- Interaction buttons appear when approaching objects.
- OPEN button for doors.
- SHOP button for shop interactions.

PC / Laptop

- WASD or arrow keys to move.
- Mouse to rotate the camera.
- E to interact.
- Mouse to navigate menus.

Use smooth third-person movement and camera following.

5. BIG CRACK LAB

Create a large building with a visible sign saying BIG CRACK LAB.

Features:

- Automatic entrance door.
- Door opens when the player presses E or taps OPEN.
- Interior upgrade shop.
- Research equipment.
- Industrial computers.
- Upgrade purchasing interface.

Available upgrades:

- Drill power.
- Drilling speed.
- Machine durability.
- Money multiplier.
- Oil efficiency.

6. Main Mining Rig

Create a large industrial drilling rig inspired by the Kola Superdeep Borehole.

Include:

- Large steel drilling tower.
- Rotating drill components.
- Metal pipes and platforms.
- Industrial control panels.
- Underground drilling animation.
- Depth measurement display.
- Machine condition indicator.

The machine must visibly drill deeper as the player progresses.

7. Oil System

Oil is required to operate the mining rig.

Every 60 seconds, the current oil supply runs out.

When oil reaches zero:

- Stop the drilling machine.
- Display an OUT OF OIL warning.
- Allow the player to purchase more oil.

Create a separate oil shop beside the mining rig.

Oil types:

- Basic Oil.
- Improved Oil.
- Advanced Oil.
- Premium Oil.

Each oil type should have different prices and efficiency.

8. Money System

Automatically reward the player every 5 seconds.

Display a money counter on the HUD.

Players can earn additional money through mining progression.

Use money to purchase:

- Laboratory upgrades.
- Drilling equipment.
- Oil.
- Machine improvements.

Make all prices configurable and balanced.

9. Security Camera System

Inside the player's base, create a security control room with a large CCTV monitor.

Allow players to interact with the monitor and switch between camera feeds.

Camera locations:

1. Main entrance.
2. Mining rig.
3. BIG CRACK LAB.
4. Oil station.
5. Underground drilling progress.
6. Outer perimeter.

Each camera must display a live view of its assigned location.

Add a camera interface showing camera names, connection status, and timestamps.

The underground camera must reveal how deep the drilling m (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable BIG CRACK LAB survival/mining game in the repository.

## Requirements
- 2.5D third-person industrial research facility on flat grassland, with lab, drilling rig, oil depot, security room, roads, fences, and environmental details.
- PC controls: WASD/arrows, mouse camera, E interaction. Mobile: joystick, camera control, contextual interactions.
- Include upgrades, drilling/depth progression, oil depletion and purchases, periodic income, day/night, power outages/monster, and six CCTV feeds.
- Make the game polished and responsive; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML/CSS/Canvas game without a framework or external game engine.
- Procedural pseudo-isometric 2.5D art and UI are used instead of imported 3D assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game page structure, HUD, mobile controls, modal containers, and responsive styling.
- Added substantial procedural Canvas scene/rendering code for the facility and player.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`: it currently ends after `buyUpgrade`; required gameplay systems and the closing IIFE are not yet present.
- Run syntax checks and test in a browser; no browser verification or screenshot has been done.

### Blocked
- `game.js` is incomplete, so the page is not yet a playable game.

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` with oil/refueling, security feeds, guide modal, HUD, update loop, input/touch controls, and final IIFE closure.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and resolve errors.
3. Launch and verify gameplay/UI in a browser; capture and inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, control and modal elements.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive/mobile layout.
- `game.js`: In-progress game implementation; currently incomplete.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- An earlier `node --check game.js` failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'`; the file was subsequently rewritten, but is currently incomplete and has not been rechecked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable BIG CRACK LAB survival/mining game in the repository.

## Requirements
- 2.5D third-person industrial research facility on grassland with a lab, drilling rig, oil depot, security room, roads, fences, and environmental details.
- PC controls: WASD/arrows, mouse camera, E interaction; mobile: joystick, camera control, contextual interactions.

- Make the game polished and responsive; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/Canvas, procedural pseudo-isometric art, and UI without a framework or external game engine.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, HUD, responsive styling, modal containers, and mobile controls.
- Expanded `game.js` with drawing helpers, roads, site buildings, interactions, upgrades, fuel purchases, six camera feeds, guide, HUD, progression, day/night, outage/monster logic, and keyboard/touch controls.

- Validate runtime/browser behavior and fix any issues.

2. Run the game in a browser, inspect the canvas/UI, and test controls, interactions, upgrades, fuel, and outage behavior.
3. Fix discovered issues, including making monster movement visible if appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, UI interactions, and controls; contains the current runtime placeholder.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements referenced by `game.js`.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.

- Changes are uncommitted; repository contains new files including `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable BIG CRACK LAB survival/mining game in the repository.

## Requirements
- Create a polished, responsive 2.5D industrial research facility with a lab, drilling rig, oil depot, security room, roads, fences, and environmental details.
- Support PC controls (WASD/arrows, mouse camera, E interaction) and mobile controls (joystick, camera, contextual interactions).
- Include upgrades, drilling and depth progression, oil purchases/depletion, periodic income, day/night, power outages/monster, and six CCTV feeds.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/Canvas with procedural pseudo-isometric art and no framework or external game engine.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, HUD, responsive styling, mobile controls, facility visuals, controls, interactions, upgrades, fuel purchases, six camera feeds, guide, progression, day/night, outages, and monster behavior.
- Added rig casing repairs in the Research Lab and paused player movement while modals are open.
- Replaced the suspected rig rendering placeholder with valid drawing code; the `...` found in the initial check was a valid spread operator.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Captured desktop and mobile headless Chromium screenshots successfully.

### Active
- Further runtime/gameplay verification and polish, including checking interaction flows and remaining game mechanics.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction automation was not available via installed Node `playwright` or `puppeteer` packages.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the captured screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/bcl-screen.png` and `/tmp/opencode/bcl-mobile.png` if needed.
2. Run additional browser-based or manual checks for controls, interactions, purchases, upgrades, repair, and outage behavior.
3. Fix any issues discovered.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, UI interactions, and controls.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements referenced by `game.js`.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- Most recent checks: `node --check game.js` passed, and headless Chromium generated screenshots without a reported page error.

- Use standalone HTML/CSS/Canvas with procedural pseudo-isometric art and no framework or external game engine.
